## How the score was worked out

Each result below implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average. Tests that separate models cleanly and agree with the other tests weigh more. A small pull toward the middle keeps thinly tested models from swinging too far. [Method](../method.md)

<pre>
source                  test                    score  implies  date        weight
<a name="paper-2211.05100v4"></a>BLOOM: A 176B-Paramet…  <a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2211.05100v4">HumanEval (lab)</a>          7.7%    44.7   2023-06-27   95% ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇
prior                   pull toward the middle           49.8                 5% ▇
                        weighted average               = 45.0
</pre>

## How to run it

<pre>
download        size  score
4-bit fp16  ~14.14GB   45.0
</pre>

```sh
# 4-bit fp16
uv run --with torch --with 'transformers<5' --with accelerate python -c "from transformers import pipeline; print(pipeline('text-generation', model='bigscience/bloom-7b1', torch_dtype='auto', device_map='auto')('Once upon a time', max_new_tokens=40)[0]['generated_text'])"
```

<sub>The score is the published model's; quantized downloads haven't been evaluated separately.</sub>
